title: Small decision-tree depth yields a narrow CNF
statement: Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $\rho$ be a restriction on the $n$ variables (fixing some coordinates to Boolean values and leaving the rest free), and write $f\!\restriction_\rho$ for the restricted function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$, obtained by evaluating $f$ with the fixed coordinates set by $\rho$ and the free coordinates supplied by $x$. If $f\!\restriction_\rho$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$, then there is a CNF formula $\psi$ whose every clause contains at most $l$ literals and which computes $f\!\restriction_\rho$ on every input, that is, $\psi(x) = f\!\restriction_\rho(x)$ for all $x \in \{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n variables
ρ is a restriction on the n variables
the restricted function f|_ρ has decision-tree depth at most l
replaced:
If the restricted function $f|_\rho$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$, then there exists a
$\mathrm{CNF}$ $\psi$ of width at most $l$ that computes $f|_\rho$ on every input.
